headline: A strong cold front sweeps through LA County Thursday morning with heavy downpours, a chance of thunderstorms and gusty winds, under a Flood Watch everywhere except the Antelope Valley, before cool, dry weather returns Friday and Saturday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: The front was crossing the Central Coast Wednesday evening (the northwest tip of San Luis Obispo County already had 1.5–3 inches, most other places a half inch or less) and will move through southern Santa Barbara and Ventura counties overnight, then through LA County, including the Glendale/Burbank area, Thursday morning and possibly early afternoon, with the most changeable conditions at Burbank from about 6 AM to noon. Rain should intensify as the front rounds Point Conception, with peak rates of a half inch per hour, areas of 0.75 inch and locally 1 inch per hour (heaviest in the Santa Barbara and western Ventura mountains); storm totals are 1–2 inches for most coast and valley areas, locally up to 3 inches, and 2–5 inches on south-facing slopes, though totals may come in a little lower than advertised. The front hasn't produced thunder yet, but there is still about a 20% chance of thunderstorms, with 2–4 hours of stormy weather possible as the strongest part passes, and a very small chance (5% or less) of a weak tornado, mainly in the LA Basin on Thursday. Gusts can reach 35 mph in lower areas and 50 mph in the mountains under Wind Advisories through Thursday morning, and a Flood Watch runs through Thursday afternoon for everywhere but the Antelope Valley, so expect slick and at times impassable streets and freeways, and avoid parking under trees.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: In the last few hours of the storm on Thursday, snow levels drop enough for 3–6 inches mainly above 7,000 feet, too high to cause much trouble. Friday and Saturday turn dry with light offshore (land-to-sea) breezes and highs mostly in the 60s. A brief area of high pressure brings sunny skies Saturday, but temperatures stay 5–10 degrees below normal.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A weak system arrives Sunday, likely bringing rain to the Central Coast (up to a quarter inch) but only about a 40% chance of rain south of Point Conception, including LA County, where amounts would stay under a tenth of an inch; highs stay in the mid 60s. Monday is dry and mostly sunny with little temperature change. Another storm looks possible later Tuesday or Wednesday, with about a 20% chance it turns into a fairly sizable system, though computer models don't agree well.

coast: Dangerous beach conditions continue into Friday, peaking Thursday, with High Surf Advisories for all beaches: large surf will bring very dangerous rip currents and hazardous jetties. Minor to moderate coastal flooding is possible, especially at Thursday morning's high tide (Coastal Flood Advisory 3–10 AM Thursday for the Central Coast), with seawater over low-lying beaches, walkways and parking lots and significant beach erosion; the Central Coast could see wave damage to piers, flooded roads and possibly structures, and large breaking waves at Morro Bay Harbor (and to a lesser extent Ventura Harbor), with waves at or over the base of the Pismo and Cayucos piers. Offshore, Gale Warnings run until 3–9 AM Thursday and Small Craft Advisories through Friday, with south gusts over 35 knots and 10–15 foot seas seen off the Central Coast Wednesday evening and possible thunderstorms over the water; winds turn northwest behind the front, showers may linger into Friday, and conditions improve Friday and turn fairly mild Saturday, with only a minor weak front Sunday into Monday. Extremely high, likely record-breaking tides arrive over Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day), and combined with new swells they will likely cause at least widespread moderate coastal flooding on all coasts, possibly significant if a bigger swell lines up with the tides.
watch_for: Heavy downpours and street/freeway flooding Thursday morning in LA County, plus about a 20% chance of thunderstorms and a small chance of a weak tornado
Whether Sunday's light rain makes it south of Point Conception (about a 40% chance)
Record high tides Thanksgiving week and a possible larger storm around Tuesday through Thanksgiving
confidence: Forecasters are confident in Thursday's storm and dangerous ocean conditions, though rain totals may run a bit lower and conditions will change quickly during the front's passage; they're confident in dry weather Friday–Saturday and less certain about next week's storm because computer models disagree.
